# 37 Practices of a Bodhisattva — Sangha Study Groups

> Peer-led study groups on Gyalse Tokme Zangpo’s fourteenth-century Tibetan Buddhist text, with the root text in three translations and commentary from seven teachers on every verse, gathered for study. Connected to Olga Kornyushyna, a Ukrainian student of Garchen Rinpoche whose wartime commentary on the text is being brought into English.

- **What is the 37 Practices of a Bodhisattva?** A fourteenth-century Tibetan Buddhist text by Gyalse Tokme Zangpo (1295–1369). In thirty-seven short verses it lays out the whole path of a bodhisattva, someone who trains to benefit all beings: from valuing this human life, through meeting harm with patience, to dedicating every virtue to others. It belongs to the lojong, or mind-training, tradition. Garchen Rinpoche calls it the heart of his teaching and recommends it to all his students.
- **Who wrote it, and where?** Gyalse Tokme Zangpo (1295–1369), a Tibetan master who lived for many years in retreat at Ngulchu. The closing verses say it was composed in Jewel Cave (Rinchen Puk) in Ngulchu, “for his own and others’ benefit.”
- **How is the text organised?** An homage and statement of purpose, 37 verses in seven parts, and closing verses. The parts are The preliminaries (1–7), The three capacities (8–10), Exchanging self and other (11), Transforming adversity (12–21), Ultimate bodhicitta (22–24), The six paramitas (25–30) and Final precepts, daily conduct (31–37).
- **Which commentaries and translations are gathered here?** Commentary from seven teachers: Garchen Rinpoche, H.H. the Dalai Lama, Dr. Alexander Berzin, Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Khenpo Sodargye, Ven. Thubten Chodron and Ken McLeod. The root text appears in three translations: Garchen Institute, Adam Pearcey and Ken McLeod. Every entry links to its source.
- **How can I study it with others?** Start a small peer-led study group. The free facilitator toolkit gives opening prayers, a ten-week format covering three or four verses a session, and guidance for leading without being a teacher. Registered groups are invited to a monthly live Q&A with Olga Kornyushyna, a Ukrainian student of Garchen Rinpoche whose wartime commentary on the text is being brought into English.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://37practices.space/): the study group initiative, the ten-week format, the monthly Q&A with Olga Kornyushyna, and her book.
- [Facilitator toolkit](https://37practices.space/toolkit.html): how to start and run a study group, prayers, curriculum, group registration.
- [All verses](https://37practices.space/verses/index.html): every verse on its own page, with an overview of the text.
- [Study the Verses](https://37practices.space/study-the-verses.html): an interactive browser for comparing commentaries verse by verse.

- [Verse 6: Cherish the spiritual teacher](https://37practices.space/verses/6.html): The preliminaries.
- [Verse 7: Take refuge in the Three Jewels](https://37practices.space/verses/7.html): The preliminaries.
- [Verse 8: Lesser capacity: karma and the lower realms](https://37practices.space/verses/8.html): The three capacities.
- [Verse 9: Middling capacity: dewdrop pleasures, changeless liberation](https://37practices.space/verses/9.html): The three capacities.
- [Verse 10: Great capacity: our mothers; arousing bodhicitta](https://37practices.space/verses/10.html): The three capacities.

- [Verse 12: When robbed: dedicate everything](https://37practices.space/verses/12.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 13: When harmed though innocent: take on their suffering](https://37practices.space/verses/13.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 14: When slandered: praise their qualities](https://37practices.space/verses/14.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 15: When publicly humiliated: see a teacher](https://37practices.space/verses/15.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 16: When betrayed by one you raised: love them more](https://37practices.space/verses/16.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 17: When treated with contempt: honor them as your teacher](https://37practices.space/verses/17.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 18: When destitute and ill: take on all beings' suffering](https://37practices.space/verses/18.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 19: When prosperous and praised: no conceit](https://37practices.space/verses/19.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 20: The real enemy: subdue your own anger](https://37practices.space/verses/20.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 21: Sense pleasures: salt water](https://37practices.space/verses/21.html): Transforming adversity.
- [Verse 22: Appearances are mind; mind is beyond fabrication](https://37practices.space/verses/22.html): Ultimate bodhicitta.
- [Verse 23: Attractive things: summer rainbows](https://37practices.space/verses/23.html): Ultimate bodhicitta.
- [Verse 24: Adversity: the death of a child in a dream](https://37practices.space/verses/24.html): Ultimate bodhicitta.
- [Verse 25: Generosity](https://37practices.space/verses/25.html): The six paramitas.

- [Verse 29: Meditative concentration](https://37practices.space/verses/29.html): The six paramitas.
- [Verse 30: Wisdom](https://37practices.space/verses/30.html): The six paramitas.
- [Verse 31: Examine your own confusion](https://37practices.space/verses/31.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 32: Don't speak of others' faults](https://37practices.space/verses/32.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 33: Give up attachment to patrons and gain](https://37practices.space/verses/33.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 34: Abandon harsh words](https://37practices.space/verses/34.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 35: Slay afflictions the moment they arise](https://37practices.space/verses/35.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 36: In everything, watch the mind, benefit others](https://37practices.space/verses/36.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.
- [Verse 37: Dedicate the merit](https://37practices.space/verses/37.html): Final precepts, daily conduct.

## Attribution

- Commentary summaries and “Across the commentaries” notes are original prose written for this study group; quotations are attributed and linked to their sources. Published books are cited as further reading only, with no text reproduced.
- Translations by Garchen Institute, Adam Pearcey and Ken McLeod, each linked to its source and licence on the verse pages.
